checks.topic: Actual polynomial subalgebra versus intermediate field
checks.detail: polyDeriv has domain Algebra.adjoin ℚ {t}, the actual polynomial subalgebra ℚ[t], and codomain K. It recovers the unique representing polynomial via the transcendental algebra equivalence, formally differentiates it and evaluates in K. The readback does not move the derivative domain to ℚ(t) or all K. The two contexts without transcendence now avoid a Chinese phrase that could falsely assert A≠F as underlying subsets.

checks.topic: formallyEtale_adjoin algebraicity binder independent of transcendence
checks.detail: The exact type has K a characteristic-zero field, an arbitrary t∈K, and the typeclass [Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ⟮t⟯ K]. It has no Transcendental hypothesis and no FiniteDimensional hypothesis. All languages retain that scope and the localization/separable-field-extension composition. In particular t can be algebraic, so ℚ[t] and ℚ(t) can have equal underlying carriers.

The declaration is defined for every t. The guard is exactly Transcendental ℚ t ∧ Algebra.IsAlgebraic ℚ⟮t⟯ K. The true branch uses its two proofs for the actual polynomial derivative and formal-etale extension; if either conjunct fails the result is the zero derivation. No unconditional derivAlong(t)(t)=1, uniqueness theorem or extra guard hypothesis is added to the statement.

The readbacks retain the fixed actual Model field, every proper valuation subring containing ℚ, all-place hDVR, transcendental ψ, regularity ψ∈P.1 and integer 1<ramIdx.
